prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1081; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe in your own words what happened on the day of the collision.

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Houston, heading toward the highway. The other car came over into my lane while it was trying to pass a slow vehicle. I braked and turned a little, but we still met nearly head-on. It was a light impact, though. Both cars were moving slowly.

Q: What was your speed at the time of impact, as best you recall?

A: I'd say maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. I was already slowing for traffic ahead.

Q: Were you wearing a seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy?

A: No. The car jolted forward and back, and I heard a loud bang, but nothing deployed.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle and speak with anyone at the scene?

A: I got out and spoke with the other driver and a police officer. The officer took down information and gave me a report number.

Q: When did you first notice you were hurt?

A: Right away I felt stiffness in my neck, but I thought it would pass. By the next morning it was a lot worse, with pain running into my shoulders and headaches.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I saw my family doctor and I've been doing physical therapy twice a week. The doctor diagnosed a neck strain and prescribed muscle relaxers.

Q: Did you have any neck problems before this collision?

A: No, nothing that required treatment. I'd had some occasional stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing like this.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I want to get back to normal as soon as possible. Thank you for listening.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
